key_insight: LLM agents struggle to reliably set up high-fidelity MBPT workflows on their own, but a knowledge-engineered, deterministic framework can make GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT calculations consistently runnable.
engineering_relevance: This work shows that expert-curated workflow knowledge and controlled execution can turn fragile agentic automation into a dependable tool for computational materials discovery and excited-state modeling.
method: Benchmarked out-of-the-box LLM agents on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow construction.
Built AI-Donkey, combining expert knowledge with deterministic execution to guide multi-step MBPT workflows.
Tested autonomous calculations and post-processing on 1D, 2D, and bulk materials.
evidence_signal: Out-of-the-box agents averaged 54% on GW, 36% on GW-BSE, and 19% on GWPT benchmarks, with large run-to-run variation; with AI-Donkey, all tested agents produced complete, runnable workflows with no observed variation.
watch_item: The framework depends on expert-curated knowledge and may require substantial domain-specific maintenance as methods, software, and workflows evolve.
paper_title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
